articles.title: From 'Bibi or Tibi' to kingmakers: Arab parties could decide Netanyahu's fate
articles.summary: For years, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu used Arab political participation as a warning to voters, famously campaigning with the slogan \"Bibi
articles.body: For years, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu used Arab political participation as a warning to voters, famously campaigning with the slogan "Bibi or Tibi". Now, the very lawmakers he once portrayed as a threat to his political future could hold the key to ending his rule, as Arab-led parties offer to back a Jewish-led opposition government following Israel's fractured election.According to a report by The Associated Press (AP), Ahmad Tibi, a senior lawmaker from the Arab-led Joint List, has offered to cooperate with opposition parties led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to remove Netanyahu from power."We want to do things that we did not do in the past in order to remove this criminal government," Tibi told AP. He said his bloc was prepared to support an opposition government without necessarily joining its governing coalition.A day earlier, on Wednesday, another Arab-led party, Mansour Abbas-led Ra'am, had also announced that it would recommend Eisenkot to Herzog to form the next government. The party's eight lawmakers joined the opposition leader's growing support base, according to The Times of Israel.The October 27 election has left Israel's 120-member Knesset without a clear majority. Netanyahu's right-wing bloc secured 53 seats, while the opposition led by Eisenkot won 48.The Joint List secured 11 seats and another Arab-led party, Ra'am, won eight. Together, the two Arab-led parties hold 19 seats, potentially taking the opposition's strength to 67, above the 61 seats required to form a government.The numbers have placed Arab lawmakers in a potentially decisive position in Israel's government formation process. The Joint List could extend parliamentary support to an opposition-led administration without taking ministerial positions or formally entering the coalition.Such an arrangement could allow Jewish-led opposition parties to form a government while relying on Arab lawmakers during crucial parliamentary votes.A break from decades of political precedentArab parties have historically remained outside Israeli governing coalitions, although Arab lawmakers have previously supported governments through parliamentary votes.A major breakthrough came in 2021, when Mansour Abbas-led Ra'am became the first independent Arab party in decades to formally join an Israeli governing coalition. It supported the government formed by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, helping end Netanyahu's 12 consecutive years in power.The Joint List, however, has traditionally maintained a more confrontational position towards Israel's political establishment. The alliance of three Arab-led parties opposes Israel's definition as a Jewish state and advocates equal rights for all citizens, alongside Palestinian statehood in the West Bank, Gaza and east Jerusalem.Its willingness to support an opposition government therefore marks a significant departure from its earlier approach.Opposition's dilemma over Arab supportDespite the possibility of securing a parliamentary majority, cooperation with Arab-led parties could prove politically difficult for Eisenkot and his allies.Some opposition figures are reluctant to depend on lawmakers whose positions on Israel's national identity, the Palestinian issue and the war in Gaza differ sharply from their own.According to The Times of Israel, Eisenkot has set four conditions for parties seeking to join his government, including recognising Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, accepting the values of its Declaration of Independence, supporting mandatory service for all citizens and recognising Hamas as a terrorist organisation that must be dismantled.However, Ahmad Tibi has argued that these conditions should not apply to the Joint List if it provides parliamentary support to an opposition government without formally joining the coalition.You use AI every day. articles.summary: India's conventional missile arsenal received another boost on Thursday as the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) successfully
articles.body: India's conventional missile arsenal received another boost on Thursday as the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) successfully flight-tested its indigenous Pralay missile off the Odisha coast. The test, conducted at 11.10 am, was part of the missile's user evaluation trials, marking another step towards strengthening India's home-grown strike capabilities.Defence minister Rajnath Singh announced the successful trial in a post on X, saying the missile met all stipulated objectives. He added that its performance was validated through data captured by various range instruments deployed during the test.The Pralay missile is an indigenously developed, solid-propellant, quasi-ballistic surface-to-surface missile with a strike range of 150 to 500 km, depending on its payload weight. It can carry a 1,000-kg payload over 350 km, while a lighter 500-kg payload extends its range to approximately 500 km.According to the defence ministry, it uses advanced guidance and navigation systems to ensure high precision and can carry multiple types of warheads to engage different targets. The missile can be launched from a mobile launcher, allowing it to be deployed from different locations.Pralay follows a quasi-ballistic trajectory, which allows it to manoeuvre during flight rather than follow a predictable ballistic path. This capability is designed to make interception by enemy air defence systems more challenging. Its solid-fuel propulsion and mobile launch platform also provide operational flexibility.

articles.title: 'Memory of the world': Rajatarangini, Mahabharata & Arthashastra get UN recognition
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Three major works of India's literary, historical and intellectual heritage, Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini', the 'Mahabharata' and Kautilya's
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Three major works of India's literary, historical and intellectual heritage, Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini', the 'Mahabharata' and Kautilya's 'Arthashastra', have been added to Unesco's Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific.The decision was taken at the 11th session of the Memory of the World Committee for Asia and the Pacific (MOWCAP), held in Jakarta, Indonesia.The development was announced by Dr Sachchidanand Joshi, member secretary of the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), which contributed to preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.In 2024, India had secured regional register recognition for three other literary works: The Ramcharitmanas, Panchatantra and Sahṛdayālokalocana.With the latest additions, India's total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six.Composed in the 12th century, Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini' provides a chronological account of Kashmir's rulers, political developments and the region's social and cultural life. Its approach to documenting history through evidence, traditions and critical inquiry gives it a distinct place in Indian historiography.The 'Mahabharata', one of the major epics of Indian civilisation, explores themes including Dharma, duty, justice, power and human relationships. Its philosophical reflections and enduring values have also made it part of South Asia's shared cultural memory.Kautilya's 'Arthashastra' deals with governance, statecraft, economic policy, diplomacy, administration and strategic affairs. The work reflects ancient India's political and administrative thinking and its understanding of the functioning of the state.The three inscriptions represent different aspects of India's intellectual traditions, spanning historical writing, philosophy and ethical thought, and governance.The announcement also comes amid efforts under the Gyan Bharatam Mission to preserve, promote and digitise India's manuscript heritage. articles.title: Rhode Island turned four-lane roads into three-lane “road diets”; a safety analysis found 29% fewer crashes and 37% fewer fatal or injury crashes
articles.summary: Rhode Island's innovative road diet approach converts four-lane roads into safer three-lane layouts, resulting in a significant reduction of 29% in total crashes and 37% in fatal or injury crashes, showcasing improvements in road safety and community wellbeing.
articles.body: Four-lane roads can create conflicts when vehicles slow down or cross traffic to turn. Rhode Island addressed these risks by converting selected roads into three-lane layouts. The changes left one through lane in each direction and added a centre lane for left turns. A state-specific evaluation found fewer crashes after the conversions, including crashes involving fatalities or injuries.Rhode Island’s evaluation found a reduction in total and injury crashesYuying Zhou, Scott Himes, Thanh Le, Jeff Gooch, Kayla Northup and Peter Pavao published Safety Effectiveness of the Road Diet Treatment in Rhode Island In Transportation Research Record in 2022. The assessment involved the installation of road diets in Rhode Island and the calculation of crash modification factors (CMFs), which are measures of change in the number of crashes that occur due to a road treatment. The results were a CMF of 0.71 for all crashes, which equates to a 29% reduction. For fatal and injury crashes, or KABC crashes, which cover fatal, incapacitating, non-incapacitating and possible injury crashes but not property damage-only crashes, the CMF was 0.63, equating to a 37% reduction.The FHWA’s Rhode Island Highway Safety Improvement Program report describes the state’s CMF development process as based on the regression cross-section method. The Rhode Island evaluation was a regression-based before-and-after analysis of road diets installed before the study’s 2022 publication, so it could not have drawn on post-installation data from the Main Avenue project, which was completed in October 2022. There is no evidence of an untreated control group or an empirical Bayes process in the summary provided.A three-lane layout separates turning vehicles from through trafficFederal guidance also defines a traditional road diet as the conversion of an undivided four-lane road into a three-lane road. The centre lane provides room for motorists to slow down before making left turns without stopping in the through lane. This helps avoid potential issues with unexpected lane changes and slowing down due to turning traffic. The available space provided by eliminating the through lane can be used for cycling lanes, pedestrian islands, transit purposes, or parking.Virginia research found similar reductions, with bicycle lanes Linda Lim and Michael D. Fontaine examined road diet safety in Development of Road Diet Segment and Intersection Crash Modification Factors, published in Transportation Research Record in 2022. The study encompassed 36 road segments and 39 intersections that had undergone road diets from 2009 to 2018. The road diets included bicycle lanes, so the results reflect the entire treatment rather than lane striping alone.In terms of road segments, the FHWA Crash Modification Factors Clearinghouse lists the Virginia study’s CMFs as 0.62 for total crashes and 0.36 for fatal and injury crashes, which correspond to reductions of 38% and 64%. For intersections, the same clearinghouse entry reports CMFs of 0.65 for total crashes and 0.54 for fatal and injury crashes, which correspond to reductions of 35% and 46%. There was no safety benefit found at unsignalized intersections. Similar to the Rhode Island Study mentioned above, the findings from the Virginia study demonstrate a reduction in the number of crashes after road diet treatments. However, since the two studies were conducted in different settings and designs, those percentages cannot be generalised.RIDOT installed a road diet on Main Avenue in Warwick The Rhode Island Department of Transportation’s (RIDOT) October 11, 2022, travel advisory stated that the agency planned to install a road diet on Main Avenue (Route 113) between Route 5 and Jefferson Boulevard in Warwick during the week of October 17, with the three-lane section running between Bailey Street and Sycamore Avenue. Bad weather delayed the work and the new traffic configuration was expected to be in place by the morning of October 20. The new road design was implemented on October 20. The agency also conducted other road diets throughout the state.RIDOT indicated speeding, crashes and narrow roads as some of its concerns. According to the review, there were 59 crashes in the previous five years, out of which one was fatal and 14 caused injuries. The new design would lead to 25 seconds of additional travel time on average. The agency stated in 2022 that it would review the project and cooperate with the City of Warwick and that this review would be conducted separately from the statewide safety analysis. The 29% and 37% reductions come from the Rhode Island evaluation and not from any post-installation results for Main Avenue.The Rhode Island findings suggest that the road diets can help reduce crashes and improve safety on roads with suitable conditions. The research from Virginia found some reduction, but in their case, they had the bicycle lanes included in the treatment. Neither study has proven that all four-lane roads will have the same outcome.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: English comedian Russell Brand, former husband of American singer Katy Perry, was on Thursday convicted of rape and sexual assault over incidents involving four women that date back more than 20 years.The 51-year-old was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. articles.title: In 2007–08, five states narrowed rural intersection approaches with rumble strips; across eight sites, crashes fell 32% and fatal or injury crashes fell 34%
articles.summary: A Federal Highway Administration study shows that installing rumble strips at rural intersections led to a 32% reduction in crashes and a 34% decrease in fatal or injury accidents in five states from 2007 to 2008. Explore how this cost-effective solution enhances road safety.
articles.body: Intersections of rural roads can cause safety hazards for drivers, especially if they drive at high speed and have very little time to notice intersections or a stop sign. For drivers on highways that have a long distance between intersections, there is a higher risk of accidents because they are less likely to see vehicles that enter the road from a secondary road. To address this issue, the Federal Highway Administration sought to reduce speeds without requiring reconstruction work.According to a June 2010 Federal Highway Administration technical report, treatment sites in Missouri, Kentucky, Pennsylvania, Florida and Maryland were part of an experiment from 2007 to 2008. As per the evaluation, there was an overall decrease of 32% in the total number of accidents and 34% in the number of accident-causing fatalities after installing the system.Why rural intersections require a different safety approachThe FHWA came up with this treatment due to the risk caused by unsignalized rural intersections. As per the statistics reported in its study, 37% of all the fatal accidents that occurred at intersections across America happened in unsignalized rural intersections. Over 90% of the accidents in such cases took place on two-lane highways, indicating the difficulties drivers face while travelling on narrow highways.In such places, no traffic signal makes motorists slow down on the main road. When drivers encounter vehicles from a side road, differences in speed and reaction time create a crash risk. This can be aggravated, especially where the intersection is not visible, or the driver cannot see any warning sign. Instead of installing a traffic light or building a roundabout, the FHWA considered a treatment that used existing road space more effectively. The purpose of this treatment was to create the illusion of narrowness on the approach, which would prompt drivers to slow down before reaching the intersection.How rumble strips changed the road layoutThe treatment included the application of rumble strips adjacent to the edges of the road as well as within the painted yellow median leading up to the intersection. This reduced the width of the smooth pavement, creating a narrow driving corridor for motorists approaching the intersection. This treatment spanned about 150 feet on both approaches to the intersection. A rumble strip is a specially designed groove or a surface pattern on pavement that creates noise and vibration when a vehicle runs over it. It is normally used to warn drivers who stray near the edges or central line of the road. In this case, however, the presence of rumble strips also helped delineate lane boundaries and slow drivers as they approached the intersection.The implementation of treatment was done in seven two-way stop-controlled intersections and one T intersection. The participating states had chosen sites where speeding, visibility problems at the intersection, or failure to stop at stop signs had been a problem. The construction cost figure varies from place to place. The cost incurred in Pennsylvania was somewhat around $50000 to $ 70,000, whereas the estimated cost in other states participating in the program was somewhere around $10,000 to $30,000.Crash figures showed a reduction after installation The treatment evaluation involved comparison of crash data before and after the treatment. The study used 3 to 5 years of pre-treatment data and at least 2 years of post- implementation data. The evaluation considered the variation in traffic volumes and the anticipated crash frequencies at similar intersections. There was an average reduction of 32% in the total number of crashes and 34% in fatal injury crashes. All eight sites experienced a reduction in crashes on a yearly basis following the treatment; however, there were different extents of improvement. The largest decrease in total crashes occurred at the second site in Pennsylvania, which was 63%. Pennsylvania's first site Had A 49% reduction in fatal and injury crashes.A study published in Accident Analysis & Prevention investigated a central line rumble strip installed on about 210 Miles of two-lane rural roads in 7 US states. The study applied an empirical Bayes before-and-after evaluation to assess any changes in crash frequency involving vehicles crossing to the opposite traffic lane. Though the research addressed a different application of rumble strips, it provided additional information regarding their possible benefit to road safety and improvement.The FHWA report noted several shortcomings, and the reductions at the eight intersections did not reach statistical significance at the 95% confidence level. Researchers explained this by a small number of sites included in the study and the variance in implementation of the treatment. They suggested adding more sites and collecting more data to test the treatment's effects. The findings gave transportation agencies a less costly option compared to reconstructing intersections. Through the use of pavement markings and rumble strips, the project showed how some changes in engineering design could be incorporated into rural road safety programs.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2020, a former homeless man in Chicago set out to feed 100 families with $2,500; six years later, Dion Dawson employs 53 people and has distributed 80,000 pounds of free, fresh produce to more than 5,400 households every week
articles.summary: Dion Dawson knows what hunger feels like and what it means to wait in line for food.
articles.body: Dion Dawson knows what hunger feels like and what it means to wait in line for food. He remembers the cold, the hours before the doors opened, and the sense that the people behind the table had already decided who he was. “You’re not treated as if you’re a person. You’re kind of a number,” he told CNN. And the food was mostly canned, processed or unhealthy. He is familiar with the struggle. In 2020, he decided to change that. The Englewood man started a non-profit called ‘Dion’s Chicago Dream’. The vision was simple: instead of giving people leftover or donated canned food, he buys fresh fruit and vegetables and delivers them directly to families. Now, the dream has grown into something bigger: he helps feed more than 5,400 households every week.As a kid, he had no favourite fruitDawson grew up in Englewood, on Chicago’s South Side. His family was often homeless, and some days they ate only once. Food pantries kept them going, but what they handed out was mostly canned goods and processed food. “I didn’t have a favourite fruit growing up,” he told the outlet. Dawson later joined the Navy and served for six years. When he came home in 2015, he was dealing with PTSD and, for a time, lived out of his car. A visit to a food pantry at a local VA hospital gave him a thought he couldn’t shake. “In 30 years, nothing had changed,” he realised. And he wanted to find a better way to feed people.Dion’s Chicago DreamIn the summer of 2020, someone asked Dawson what he planned to do for Juneteenth, as reported by National Geographic. He said he would feed 100 families, but he had no idea how. He started a GoFundMe, raised $2,500 and fed 96 families. That August, he officially launched Dion’s Chicago Dream as a non-profit.Most pantries depend on donated shelf-stable food. But Dawson’s group is different. It buys produce from local farmers and a regional supplier, which allows it to control quality. The boxes are packed six days a week, loaded into vans at 4 a.m. and delivered to homes or to Dream Vaults, locker-style collection points inside local stores. A platform called Cosmic Crate tracks each step, and recipients receive text alerts about their deliveries. “Think along the lines of HelloFresh but free,” Dawson told the outlet.The fruit and vegetables are chosen to look appealing so that people will actually want to cook with them. “It’s bright, it’s beautiful. And all of that is intentional. We want you to feel compelled to use it and to eat it.”The group doesn’t use volunteers. Its Dream Team, now more than 50 people, earns at least $20 an hour. Dawson says paid staff make for a steadier workforce and keep money in the neighbourhood.The whole programme is designed to be efficient and to treat residents with dignity. “Dion’s Chicago Dream is about meeting people where they are,” Dawson said.What started as a mission to feed 100 people has now grown into a real lifeline for thousands of families. Dion’s Chicago Dream now delivers 80,000 pounds of free, fresh produce to more than 5,400 households every week. In 2022, Dawson received an $80,000 fellowship from Echoing Green, which he said would help expand the non-profit. The group now works with healthcare systems on medically tailored boxes for patients with heart disease and diabetes. Those patients have reported lower blood sugar and weight loss, and Dawson says he has seen real changes in their lives. The kind of change he wished to see.You use AI every day. articles.title: Tsutomu Yamaguchi was in Hiroshima on business when the atomic bomb fell on August 6, 1945; he went home to Nagasaki and was hit by the second bomb three days later, survived both, and lived until 2010, aged 93
articles.summary: On August 6, 1945, Tsutomu Yamaguchi was preparing to leave Hiroshima and return to his family in Nagasaki when a blinding flash lit up the sky.
articles.body: On August 6, 1945, Tsutomu Yamaguchi was preparing to leave Hiroshima and return to his family in Nagasaki when a blinding flash lit up the sky. The 29-year-old engineer was on a business assignment for Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, working on the design of oil tankers. Within seconds, the city was devastated by the world's first atomic bomb used in warfare. Yamaguchi was thrown into the air, temporarily lost his sight and hearing, and suffered severe burns across his upper body.He managed to reach a railway station and spent the night in Hiroshima before making the journey back to Nagasaki. He had survived an atomic bombing and was finally home with his wife, Hisako, and their infant son. But the ordeal was far from over. Three days later, on August 9, as he reported for work and attempted to explain to his colleagues what he had witnessed, a second atomic bomb exploded over his hometown.Yamaguchi was among the people caught in both attacks. He survived the Hiroshima bombing and then the Nagasaki bombing, becoming the only person officially recognised by the Japanese government as a survivor of both. His story, however, was not one he readily shared for much of his life. It took decades for him to speak publicly about the experience, and he eventually became an advocate for a world without nuclear weapons.'I thought the mushroom cloud had followed me'Yamaguchi was approximately three kilometres from ground zero in Hiroshima when the bomb, code-named Little Boy, detonated at 8:15 am. In an interview with ABC News in 2009, he recalled seeing a flash and hearing an enormous sound. "I thought the sun had fallen from the sky," he said, describing the moment the explosion struck. His hair and face were burned, as was his upper body. He later recalled that only his legs remained capable of moving properly.After spending the night in Hiroshima, he managed to make his way back to Nagasaki on August 8. His injuries were treated, and his body was wrapped in bandages. Despite his condition, he returned to work the following morning. That was when the second explosion came. Yamaguchi was recounting the devastation in Hiroshima to his supervisor when another blinding flash filled the room. The United States had dropped the Fat Man atomic bomb over Nagasaki at 11:02 am on August 9."I thought the mushroom cloud had followed me from Hiroshima," he later recalled, describing his reaction to the second blast. He was around three kilometres from the Nagasaki explosion's epicentre. His wife and young son also survived. The two bombings killed tens of thousands of people immediately and left many more suffering from burns, injuries and radiation-related illnesses. Yamaguchi himself experienced lasting health problems, including hearing loss in his left ear, according to contemporary reports.Why he stayed silent for decadesAlthough his experience was extraordinary, Yamaguchi returned to his career after the war, working as an interpreter for the occupying US forces before becoming an English teacher and eventually resuming his engineering work at Mitsubishi. He also wrote poetry, including traditional Japanese tanka, and tried to rebuild an ordinary family life.His reluctance to speak about the bombings was partly rooted in the suffering he had witnessed around him. He felt uncomfortable drawing attention to his survival when so many people around him had become seriously ill or died. His daughter Toshiko Yamasaki later explained that the family had also worried that his relatively healthy appearance might lead people to underestimate the devastating effects of radiation exposure.According to ABC's 2025 retrospective, Yamaguchi began speaking publicly about his experiences around 2005, after the death of his second son, who had survived the Nagasaki bombing as an infant but later died of cancer. His memories, once kept largely within the family, became part of a wider effort to preserve the experiences of atomic bomb survivors.He travelled to the United Nations in 2006 and spoke about nuclear disarmament. His message was shaped not by a desire to be remembered as a statistical exception, but by the belief that no one should have to experience what he had.Officially recognised as a survivor of both bombingsFor years, Yamaguchi had been officially certified as a hibakusha, the Japanese term for people affected by the atomic bombings. But his government record initially recognised his exposure in Nagasaki, not Hiroshima. That changed in March 2009, when Japanese authorities officially recognised him as a survivor of both attacks. At 93, he became the first person to receive this distinction."My double radiation exposure is now an official government record. It can tell the younger generation the horrifying history of the atomic bombings even after I die," he said, according to a report by The Japan Times.Historians estimate that around 165 people may have been present in both cities during the attacks. Yamaguchi, however, remained the only person officially recognised by the Japanese government as a survivor of both. He died in Nagasaki on January 4, 2010, aged 93, after being hospitalised with stomach cancer. His death was mourned by Nagasaki's mayor, Tomihisa Taue, who described him as a valuable witness whose experiences had helped make the horrors of nuclear warfare known to the world.You use AI every day. articles.title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assaults; actor being investigated over more rape allegations
articles.summary: A jury found the actor guilty on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
articles.body:
A jury in London has found comedian and actor Russell Brand guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

The actor had been charged on seven counts: three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one count of attempted indecent assault.

After the verdict, London's Metropolitan Police Service told Yahoo that Brand, 51, is facing further allegations of rape from two women.

"The suspect has previously been interviewed under caution in connection with the allegations," the force said in a statement. "Files have been submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service in relation to both complainants." Brand has not been charged in relation to these claims.

Following a four-week trial at Southwark Crown Court in London, the jury found Brand guilty on four of the charges. He was acquitted of two rape counts and one count of attempted indecent assault.

Brand is due to be sentenced at Southwark Crown Court on Monday, Nov. 9. The judge said he should expect a lengthy prison term.

Brand became a household name in the U.K. in the 2000s as a comedian and broadcaster. He went on to star in the movies Get Him to the Greek in 2010 and Arthur the following year.

He married singer Katy Perry in October 2010, but Brand filed for divorce in December 2011, citing irreconcilable differences. Their divorce was finalized in July 2012.

The claims against Brand were made by six different women, and span from 1999-2009.

Brand had denied the charges and said he had never forced anyone to do something against their will.

Following the verdict, the judge told Brand he would be remanded in custody.

"You've been convicted of a number of offences including rape," Mr Justice Bennathan said. "The consequence of that is inevitably a significant custodial term. My current view is that I therefore have to remand you into custody."

In a statement, Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy, from London's Metropolitan Police Service, said: "Today's verdict is first and foremost a testament to the extraordinary courage, resilience and determination of the women who came forward and reported what happened to them."

The statement added: "Brand used his influence, status and fame to exploit and sexually offend against women.

"As his profile grew, so too did his sense of entitlement. I hope this conviction sends a clear message that no one is above the law, no matter how famous or powerful they may be."

Ron Brand, Russell's father, told the BBC he was "shocked" by the verdicts. "I just didn't expect this - it's wrong," he said. "It's devastating."

articles.title: A couple bought Arkansas land together, divorced within a year and each kept half; when the woman later went bankrupt, her share was sold to an investor and her ex-husband's appeal was dismissed
articles.summary: A man in Arkansas has lost his legal challenge against the sale of a property he once owned with his former wife.
articles.body: A man in Arkansas has lost his legal challenge against the sale of a property he once owned with his former wife. The couple had bought the land together in 2021 but divorced less than a year later, leaving each with a 50% share. The dispute began after the woman and her new husband filed for bankruptcy in 2023, leading to the sale of her share to an investment company.Logan Riffenburg and his former wife, Vanessa Roper, bought the property in Mountain View, Arkansas. After their divorce, both continued to own half of the land. Roper later remarried, and she and her new husband filed for bankruptcy.According to the ruling, during the bankruptcy proceedings, the trustee handling Roper's assets sought permission to sell her share of the property to Blue Sun Capital LLC. Riffenburg objected, but the bankruptcy court approved the sale, saying it was "in good faith, for fair value, and in the best interest of all parties".Riffenburg then challenged the decision and asked the court to stop the sale while his appeal was being considered. His request was rejected, and the trustee went ahead with the transaction. The trustee later argued that since the sale had been completed, Riffenburg's appeal could no longer be considered.Why former husband challenge sale?After the bankruptcy court approved the transaction, Riffenburg approached the Bankruptcy Appellate Panel for the Eighth Circuit. He wanted the panel to review the decision and also asked it to temporarily stop the sale until his appeal was decided.The bankruptcy court had already rejected his request to pause the transaction. Months later, he renewed his request before the appeals panel. However, while the request was still pending, the trustee asked the panel to dismiss his appeal, saying the sale had already been completed.The trustee relied on a provision of US bankruptcy law that protects certain completed property sales. Under this rule, a sale approved during bankruptcy proceedings generally cannot be reversed if it was made to a good-faith buyer and no court order had stopped the transaction while an appeal was pending.A divided panel accepted the trustee's argument and dismissed Riffenburg's appeal. It also rejected his request to stop the sale because the transaction had already been completed.Riffenburg then approached the US Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit, asking it to overturn the dismissal.Why federal appeals court rejected his challenge?The federal appeals court focused on whether Riffenburg had questioned the investment company's conduct when the sale was first considered by the bankruptcy court.The judges found that he had objected to the trustee's decision to sell Roper's share but had never directly challenged whether Blue Sun Capital was a good-faith buyer.This became important because an earlier ruling by the same appeals court had established that anyone opposing a bankruptcy sale must raise concerns about the buyer's good faith before the bankruptcy court. They cannot wait until a later appeal to introduce that objection.The court relied on a 2001 decision. In that case, a person opposing a property sale had questioned whether the buyer had acted honestly, but had failed to raise the issue before the bankruptcy court. The appeals court had ruled that the objection could not be considered later.Applying the same reasoning, the judges said Riffenburg's failure to question Blue Sun Capital's good faith during the original proceedings was enough to dismiss his appeal.Riffenburg argued that the bankruptcy court had required him to present evidence of wrongdoing before the trustee presented its own evidence. He said his objection to this procedure had been rejected.However, the appeals court said that objecting to the order in which evidence was presented was not the same as directly questioning the buyer's good faith. It added that Riffenburg had an opportunity to present evidence against the buyer but had not used it.Court discusses SC ruling and earlier decisionRiffenburg also appeared to rely on a 2023 US Supreme Court decision, MOAC Mall Holdings LLC v. Transform Holdco LLC. The ruling clarified that the provision protecting completed bankruptcy sales was not a jurisdictional rule.The appeals court, however, said the Supreme Court's decision did not overturn the relevant part of its 2001 ruling. It explained that the earlier requirement to challenge a buyer's good faith before the bankruptcy court remained applicable.The judgment also referred to Judge Norton's dissenting opinion when the Bankruptcy Appellate Panel dismissed Riffenburg's appeal. She had acknowledged that Riffenburg did not challenge the buyer's good faith during the earlier proceedings. However, she believed the Supreme Court's 2023 decision had changed the legal position and that the appeal should not have been dismissed.The Eighth Circuit disagreed with her interpretation and said it remained bound by the earlier ruling.Appeals court's concern about buyer's good faith findingWhile dismissing the appeal, the federal court also raised questions about the way the original sale had been approved.It noted that the bankruptcy court had not made a specific finding about whether Blue Sun Capital was a good-faith buyer. The appeals court said this was an important factual question that should ordinarily be decided by the bankruptcy court.It also referred to a decision by another federal appeals court that required bankruptcy courts to make an explicit finding about a buyer's good faith when approving the sale of assets.The Eighth Circuit said it had doubts about whether its earlier approach was consistent with the wording of the law. However, it could not depart from the precedent it was required to follow.The court also observed that changing its approach might not have affected the final outcome in this case because there was no real dispute between the parties about the buyer's good faith.The US Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit ultimately upheld the decision to dismiss Riffenburg's appeal as moot.You use AI every day. articles.title: JD(U) discusses reasons for poor show in council polls
articles.summary: JD(U) reviewed why three of four candidates lost Bihar legislative council polls; Sanjay Kumar Jha heard complaints, while BJP’s alleged role wasn’t discussed.
articles.body: Patna: The JD(U) leadership on Thursday reviewed the reasons behind the defeat of three of its four candidates in the recent legislative council elections, hearing presentations from the losing nominees and other party functionaries. The party’s working president, Sanjay Kumar Jha, took note of the concerns raised with the final decision on complaints and issues left to him.The defeated candidates were Tirhut Graduates’ seat nominee Abhishek Jha, Saran Teachers’ seat contestant Pushkar Anand and Darbhanga Teachers’ seat candidate Ghanshyam Rai. Only Neeraj Kumar, a three-time MLC from the Patna Graduates’ seat, retained his seat despite a campaign against him by the party’s Mokama MLA Anant Singh, who has since been expelled.Abhishek and Anand lost to Independent candidates Bansidhar Brajvasi and Rahul Raj. Both subsequently announced their support for the BJP. Their move fuelled speculation about the BJP’s role in the defeats.“We presented the facts and figures on the reasons behind our defeats, and we received patient hearing at the review meeting. Others, too, made their own presentations. Our working president took note of the concerns expressed,” Abhishek told reporters. He said the party’s working president would take the final decision on the complaints and issues raised.Asked whether the two Independent MLCs support for the BJP was discussed, Abhishek said the issue did not figure at the meeting. “The NDA is intact and united,” he said.Before the meeting, JD(U) state president Umesh Singh Kushwaha said the Bihar NDA was two decades old and the JD(U)-BJP partnership remained strong.The meeting was attended by Jha, Kushwaha, chief whip in the assembly Manjit Kumar Singh, the party’s winning and losing candidates, MLAs, MLCs, district presidents and constituency incharges.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.title: SC asks Anant to surrender by Dec 4 in murder case
articles.summary: Supreme Court suspends Mokama MLA Anant Singh’s bail in Dularchand Yadav murder case, orders surrender by Dec 4, 2026; probe to finish in 4 months.
articles.body: Patna: The Supreme Court on Thursday suspended Mokama MLA Anant Singh’s bail in the Dularchand Yadav murder case and directed him to surrender before the investigating officer by Dec 4, 2026, extending the earlier deadline of Dec 1. The Patna high court’s March 19, 2026, bail order will remain suspended until the next hearing.Questioning the grounds for granting bail, the apex court observed that the number of criminal cases against Singh and the seriousness of the allegations had not been adequately considered. It also questioned the approach of attributing the cases against him to political rivalry.The court directed the investigating officer to complete the probe within four months and file a supplementary chargesheet. The case will be heard again after that period.Recounting the events of Oct 30, 2025, Singh had recently said, “I had left with his supporters and convoy after having lunch. The incident took place in the Mokama assembly constituency, where Yadav’s house was located in Tartad village.”He claimed several people and vehicles were part of the convoy. While some vehicles had moved ahead, others were trailing behind. articles.title: Cloth on cam, woman strangles mother-in-law
articles.summary: Haryana’s Fatehabad police arrested Kiran for allegedly strangling her mother-in-law in Pirthala; CCTV was reportedly covered. Probe ongoing.
articles.body: Hisar: Police in Haryana’s Fatehabad district have arrested a woman for her alleged role in the murder of her mother-in-law in Pirthala village near Tohana.The suspect, identified as Kiran, wife of Pradeep Kumar, was taken into custody following a complaint filed by her father-in-law, Hawa Singh.According to police, the victim, Leela Devi, retired to her room on the night of Nov 1. Her son found her unresponsive the next morning. Family members noticed injuries and bluish discoloration around her neck, pointing to death by strangulation.The complainant alleged that a cloth was placed over the home’s CCTV camera to obscure footage and accused Kiran of carrying out the killing along with an accomplice.Sadar Tohana police SHO Sadhuram said a murder case was registered on Nov 2 under Section 103(1) of BNS.
